footer: RoadSoft Import Application — Client IT Specification — v2.2.0
subtitle: IT Specification — Version 2.2.0
purpose: Automated synchronization of digital tachograph files (`.ddd`, `.esm`) to the RoadSoft cloud platform
privileges_value: No administrator or root privileges required
important_peruser: RoadSoft installs per user account by default (AppData\Local\Programs), but the installation directory can be changed during setup. Note that user data (configuration, logs) is always stored per user account in AppData\Roaming.
note_hidden: The `AppData` folder is hidden by default in Windows. Enable "Show hidden files" in File Explorer to access it.
file_processing_intro: A file is relocated once the RoadSoft platform has given its final result. Top-level `.ddd`/`.esm` files are moved individually; a file inside a subfolder is moved on its own, keeping its relative path under `Archived/` or `Failed/`; the folder itself stays where it is. A file that is uploaded and still being processed, or that could not be sent yet, stays in the folder. Corrupted `.zip` archives are moved to `Failed/` during the initial scan.
archived_contents: Files the RoadSoft platform has imported
failed_contents: Files the RoadSoft platform refused, files set aside after repeated send failures, and corrupted archives
note_file_processing: Both folders are created automatically inside the selected sync folder. They are excluded from future scans, so files placed there will not be re-processed.
note_zip_trash: After a `.zip` archive is successfully extracted, the original `.zip` file is automatically moved to the OS recycle bin and can be restored from there if needed.
upload_history_intro: Every file is identified by a fingerprint of its contents. Before each upload the application asks the RoadSoft platform which files it already holds or has refused, and uploads only the rest. After each upload it retrieves the result. All of this is recorded in the local upload history.
upload_history_refused: A file the platform refused is kept in the history together with the platform's reason, shown in the Status column, and is not uploaded again.
upload_history_transport: A file that could not be sent because of a network or server error stays in the folder and is tried again on the following synchronizations; after three failed attempts it is set aside with the last error.
upload_history_duplicate: A copy of a file that is already in the history — under another name or in another folder — is not uploaded again.
upload_history_reset: The Reset history button clears the upload history. On the next synchronization every file in the folder is checked with the platform again: files the platform already holds are skipped, files it refused are offered once more. No files on disk are changed.
note_upload_history: The upload history is what prevents a file from being uploaded twice — not the `Archived/` folder. If the move into `Archived/` fails (for example on a network drive or a synchronized folder), the file is still not uploaded again.
autolaunch: Auto-launch on system startup is supported and configurable within the application
tray: Minimize to system tray is supported (optional)
